newsitem.title: USA: Expert identifies truck used in Oklahoma bombing.
newsitem.headline: Expert identifies truck used in Oklahoma bombing.

text.p: A vehicle expert, testifying in the Oklahoma City bombing trial Thursday, identified the vehicle used in the April 1995 attack as a Ford truck owned by the Ryder rental company.

"I believe that there was only one vehicle used in the Oklahoma City bombing. That vehicle built for and sold to Ryder had a specific and unique vehicle identification number," Edward Paddock told the court.

Paddock read out the unique 17-digit vehicle identification number, which matched the number of the truck the prosecution says was rented by accused bomber Timothy McVeigh from a firm in Junction City, Kansas, two days before the bombing of the federal government building in Oklahoma City that killed 168 people.
Paddock said he based his conclusions on a review of parts obtained at the crime scene, an analysis relative to those parts, the Ryder purchase order and an invoice from Ford.

Paddock showed the jury a photograph of the recovered parts that were reconstructed at the FBI laboratory in Washington, D.C., but pointed out that there was a gap between the rear axle and the cab portion because those parts were not recovered.

Paddock, an engineer who worked for 34 years for Ford, compared for the jury the twisted pieces recovered from the bomb site with identical, but intact, pieces taken from a Ford truck that was next off the assembly line to the one allegedly used in the bombing.
